title: བཀའ་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འབུམ། ཅ (Derge Kangyur, vol. 81)
shelf_note: Derge Kangyur rgyud 'bum vol. ca (LoC copy, BDRC scan). The pages hold the Vajramālā (rdo rje phreng ba, chapters 21 and 41 end on pp. 465 and 495) and a vajra-nectar tantra (ch. 9 ends p. 50). These belong in a Kangyur volume. No collections are set in catalog_metadata.
structure_note: 614 records, all with OCR, 162 translated (26%). Book is visible:false. with_printed_number is 0, but the leaves do carry a folio (volume letter and Tibetan folio numeral) in the left margin. The OCR does not capture it, so the counts cannot test leaf order. Each transcription is a page-aligned slice of the eSukhia Derge e-text (engine esukhia-derge-kangyur). The page breaks match the image line for line on all four pages.

tr_errors.english: The empowered skull of flesh is held with khatvargas
tr_errors.problem: garbled: the line says all [the goddesses] hold khaṭvāṅgas. The English makes a 'skull of flesh' the object and misspells khaṭvāṅga

tr_errors.english: Fill a skull cup shaped like a crescent or a bow
tr_errors.problem: the crescent/bow shape belongs to the mandala ('called skull'), not to a skull cup

tr_errors.english: of the laborer class
tr_errors.problem: caṇḍālī (outcaste) softened to 'laborer class'

tr_errors.english: spiritual attainment <note>original: <term>siddhi</term></note>
tr_errors.problem: the note labels the Sanskrit as the 'original'. The page is Tibetan (dngos grub)

other.note: translation ends with '<unclear>...</unclear>', but the OCR is not unclear: the line simply runs on to the next page (ཞགས་)

tr_errors.english: is the Jñanasattva Vajrasattva. He is spoken of as the Samayasattva
tr_errors.problem: the line lists three sattvas (jñāna-, vajra-, samaya-). The English equates them and makes Vajrasattva 'the Samayasattva'

tr_errors.english: the actual basis of the three times
tr_errors.problem: ལན་གསུམ is 'three repetitions', not the three times (past/present/future)

tr_errors.english: the conceptual thoughts of <note>sentient beings</note>
tr_errors.problem: the page opens mid-word (the subject is on the previous leaf). The note supplies 'sentient beings' as if read

tr_errors.english: These are the five peaks of speech
tr_errors.problem: 'the uttered [syllables] are the five peaks' becomes 'peaks of speech'

tr_errors.english: Great Being <note>original: "Sempa nyi", likely referring to a Bodhisattva or the practitioner as a Diamond Being</note>, now I shall further explain
tr_errors.problem: the tail of the previous leaf's sentence ('…is the very sattva') becomes an invented vocative 'Great Being', propped up by a speculative note

tr_errors.english: Just as something burnt by fire becomes non-existent and dissolves without a cause, the life-sustaining wind rises again.
tr_errors.problem: two clauses are fused, so the simile seems to cause the wind's re-arising

book_verdict: The right text on the right leaves: the eSukhia Derge e-text, sliced to match each scanned folio. The AI English is a serviceable working translation of the Vajramālā with a few loose tantric renderings and some speculative notes. Only a quarter of the volume is translated.
reader_summary: This is the Derge block print of Kangyur tantra volume ca, mostly the Vajramālā explanatory tantra, with an e-text transcription that matches each scanned folio. The English is an unrevised AI translation: it follows the verse closely, but slips on technical lists (the three sattvas, the goddesses' attributes) and adds glosses of its own. Read it as a guide to the Tibetan, not a citable rendering. About a quarter of the pages are translated.

title: བཀའ་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འབུམ། ན (Derge Kangyur, vol. 88)
shelf_note: Derge Kangyur rgyud 'bum vol. na. The sampled pages are a dhāraṇī sūtra: the stūpa that bursts from the earth, the Bodhigarbhālaṅkāralakṣa dhāraṇī, the city of Pathari, Vajrapāṇi and Mañjuśrī, and a mantra list with its sādhana. These belong in the Kangyur.

The OCR is a page-aligned slice of the eSukhia Derge e-text and matches the image line for line. The marginal folio numbers are not captured (with_printed_number 0).

book_verdict: Clean: the right text on every leaf, and the English is close and readable. The visible defect is e-text variant braces left in the Tibetan pane. Only 5% is translated.
reader_summary: This is the Derge block print of Kangyur tantra volume na. The sampled pages come from a dhāraṇī sūtra on stūpas and the Bodhigarbhālaṅkāralakṣa spell, and the e-text transcription matches the scanned folios. The English on the translated pages is accurate and plain. Only the first few dozen pages are translated, and the Tibetan pane sometimes shows the e-text's {variant,correction} braces.

title: བཀའ་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། མདོ་སྡེ། ཨཱཾཿ (Derge Kangyur, vol. 76)
shelf_note: Derge Kangyur mdo sde vol. aṃ. The sampled pages are a prophecy of the Dharma's decline: three foreign kings (Yavana, Bahlika, Śakuna), King Duṣprasaha of Kauśāmbī, and the last council where the monks kill one another. This is a sūtra-section text and belongs here.

The OCR is the page-aligned eSukhia e-text and matches the images. The marginal folio numbers are not captured.

book_verdict: The text is right and the narrative English is good, but just 8 of 578 pages are translated. Those 8 are the decline prophecy around pp. 433–439. E-text braces show in the Tibetan pane.
reader_summary: This is the Derge block print of the last sūtra-section volume, aṃ. The translated stretch is a prophecy of the end of the Dharma: foreign kings, King Duṣprasaha and the final council at Kauśāmbī. The transcription is the right text for each leaf, and the English tells the story faithfully. Almost all of the volume is Tibetan only, and the Tibetan pane shows editorial braces from the e-text.

title: བཀའ་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འབུམ། ཐ (Derge Kangyur, vol. 86)
shelf_note: Derge Kangyur rgyud 'bum vol. tha. The sampled pages are a yoga-tantra maṇḍala text: initiation, goddesses and messengers placed by direction, and a praise followed by Samantabhadra's samādhi on the 'Secret Ornament'. These belong here.
structure_note: 641 records, all with OCR, 73 translated (11%). Book is visible:false. The OCR is the page-aligned eSukhia e-text and matches the images on all four pages. The marginal folio numbers are not captured (with_printed_number 0).

book_verdict: The right text on every leaf. The English is good on the praise (239) and adequate on the ritual pages, but it blurs the maṇḍala's figures (a pāramitā goddess read as a gesture) and adds 'original:' notes that are not original. E-text braces show in the Tibetan pane.
reader_summary: This is the Derge block print of Kangyur tantra volume tha, a yoga-tantra maṇḍala and initiation text, and the transcription is the right text for each leaf. The AI English carries the ritual sequence and the praises well. In the iconographic lists, which goddess sits where is sometimes muddled, and some notes are the model's guesses. Check any identification against the Tibetan before citing it.
